request_checks.order: A1 B1 B2 A2 A3 B3 (A = numbers only, B = numbers + image)

findings: All six observations say the position of the maximum speed is unknown and give no coordinates, so no position error can be computed; the automatic scorer marks all six unscorable.

B1, B2 and B3 say in possible_interpretation that high velocity is concentrated near x=0.00 m. The reference x is 0.000538 m, which rounds to 0.00 m, but no y is given, the same answers say exact coordinates are not provided, and the scorer reads observations only. This does not show that the image was read.
A2 and A3 (numbers only) say the image does not provide coordinates, although no image was sent. The system prompt mentions an optional PNG in both conditions.

A2 and A3 read the leading energy fraction of Ux as a dominant flow direction along x. The fraction is 0.99997 for Ux and 0.999913 for Uy; the system prompt describes it as a dominant numeric pattern, and it says nothing about direction.

Every answer has 52 to 54 words; the prompt asks for under 45 English words in total. The output validator checks the three fields and the 160-character limit only. The 2026-10-17 E2B answers had 28 to 34 words.
B1, B2 and B3 are the same text, and so are A2 and A3; A1, the first request on an empty prompt cache, differs.
No answer contradicts the numeric evidence: the quoted maximum speed (82.5275 or 82.53 m/s) is the input value.
